claims.quote: monoallelic loss-of-function variants in the SCN1A gene.
AAV9-REGABA-eTFSCN1A was engineered to upregulate SCN1A expression levels within GABAergic inhibitory interneurons to correct the underlying haploinsufficiency and circuit dysfunction.

claims.object_text: alpha subunit of the voltage-gated type I sodium channel (NaV1.1) responsible for generation of action potentials in GABAergic inhibitory interneurons
claims.quote: SCN1A encodes for the alpha subunit of the voltage-gated type I sodium channel (NaV1.1), the primary voltage-gated sodium channel responsible for generation of action potentials in GABAergic inhibitory interneurons.

claims.object_text: increased SCN1A mRNA transcripts and NaV1.1 protein levels
claims.quote: led to increased SCN1A mRNA transcripts, specifically within GABAergic inhibitory interneurons, and NaV1.1 protein levels in the brain.

claims.object_text: decrease in spontaneous and hyperthermia-induced seizures and prolonged survival
claims.quote: This was associated with a significant decrease in the occurrence of spontaneous and hyperthermia-induced seizures, and prolonged survival for over a year.

claims.object_text: widespread vector biodistribution and transgene expression throughout the brain including hippocampus and cortex
claims.quote: delivery of AAV9-REGABA-eTFSCN1A by unilateral ICV injection led to widespread vector biodistribution and transgene expression throughout the brain, including key structures involved in epilepsy and cognitive behaviors, such as hippocampus and cortex.

claims.object_text: well tolerated in nonhuman primates (no adverse events, no adverse histopathology findings, no dorsal root ganglion-related toxicity)
claims.quote: AAV9-REGABA-eTFSCN1A was well tolerated, with no adverse events during administration, no detectable changes in clinical observations, no adverse findings in histopathology, and no dorsal root ganglion-related toxicity.
